gaps.sentence: If you want a refund, you ___ keep the receipt — no receipt, no refund.
gaps.hint: a necessity that applies in the future
gaps.explanation: Future necessity uses 'will have to': will have to keep.

gaps.sentence: I ___ to wear a uniform at my last job, and I hated it.
gaps.hint: an obligation imposed in the past
gaps.explanation: Past obligation is expressed with 'had to': had to wear.

gaps.sentence: He ___ have missed the train — he left home two hours early.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' expresses near-certainty that something did not happen: can't have missed.

gaps.sentence: Where is Anna? I am not sure — she ___ be in the library.
gaps.hint: an uncertain possibility, not really sure
gaps.explanation: 'Might' expresses a possibility the speaker is unsure about: might be.

gaps.sentence: I ___ rather stay at home tonight, if that is all right.
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather' expresses preference: would rather stay.

gaps.sentence: I ___ have known you were in hospital — nobody told me.
gaps.explanation: 'Couldn't have' means it was impossible to do: couldn't have known.

gaps.sentence: You ___ told me — I would have kept the evening free!
gaps.explanation: 'Should have' plus the participle criticizes something that did not happen: should have told.

gaps.sentence: You ___ have seen a ghost — there is no such thing!
gaps.hint: a past claim rejected as impossible
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' rejects a past claim as impossible: can't have seen.
